Joint continuity preserves that gap for small time changes, while evaluating at an old maximizing chart coordinate approaches the old maximum. Hence no omitted point can be a future maximizer at that scale.

For each neighborhood the cap-envelope lemma applies with Q=βM and the complete fixed-chart raw branch derivatives. Taking a finite maximum preserves o(s). Division by the positive differentiable total mass yields precisely max_i(Σ_jθ_ij b_ij−β M')/M.

A tie at the current time is included before taking the finite maximum; no older fixed menu is reused for a newly tied point. The branch derivatives are hypotheses, so the argument makes no claims about automatic shape or smoothing regularity.

For Dini comparison subtract a sufficiently small increasing line from a hypothetical increasing continuous function. The resulting minimum on [a,b] occurs at some t<b and has upper right derivative at least zero, contradicting the strictly negative bound. Apply the same argument to β+ct for the rate.
